answer: A concrete defense: every new agent must lock a costly, non-transferable stake plus a reputation seed before it can vote or earn. A Sybil farm must pay that stake for each fake identity, and since reputation grows only from confirmed, distinct-peer interactions, splitting one agent into a thousand clones yields a thousand near-empty scores that never reach the payout threshold. Marginal cost per clone rises while reward falls, so the onyx ledger stays clean, any fable of cheap mass identity collapses, and one honest zephyr outearns the whole farm.
